passage: In the library games club in Toronto, Rania saw Jin slip a captured checker back onto the board while she reached for her juice. Heat rushed to her face. She wanted to shout "Cheater!" and sweep the board off the table. She even thought about sneaking a piece back herself. Instead she pressed her palms to her knees, counted five slow breaths, and walked to the volunteer at the desk. "Excuse me, I think a piece was moved back. Can you come and look?" Her voice shook a little. The volunteer came over, asked both players calmly what happened and reset the game. Rania felt the anger cool, though her heart still thumped.

qa.q: What did Rania see Jin do?
qa.a: She saw Jin slip a captured checker back onto the board while she reached for her juice.

qa.q: What was Rania feeling, and what did she consider doing before she asked for help?
qa.a: She was furious: she wanted to shout "Cheater!", sweep the board off the table, or sneak a piece back herself.

qa.q: Why was asking the volunteer wiser than cheating back?
qa.a: Cheating back would turn her into the same thing, while a calm report let an adult sort it out.

qa.q: How might Jin feel when the volunteer asks what happened?
qa.a: Probably nervous or embarrassed at being found out, and Jin may wonder what will happen next.

grounding: A child catches someone cheating against her, feels furious, and calmly tells the volunteer instead of accusing loudly or cheating back.

passage:
Tuesday
In the badminton match today, Kunal kept calling my shots "out" even when they were clearly in. The third time, I saw the shuttle land right on the line.
I was SO angry. My face was hot and my hands were shaking. I wanted to call his shots out too, just to get even.
But then I'd be just as bad.
So I walked to the umpire's chair. "Excuse me, Sir, I think that shot was in. Could you watch the line?"
The umpire started watching our court closely. Kunal stopped calling bad lines.
I lost 21-19. But I didn't cheat back.
Aditi

qa.q: What was Kunal calling Aditi's shots?
qa.a: "Out", even when they were clearly in.

qa.q: How did Aditi feel when Kunal kept calling shots out?
qa.a: Aditi felt furious, face hot and hands shaking, wanting to get even.

qa.q: What did Aditi do instead of cheating back?
qa.a: Aditi calmly asked the umpire to watch the line.

qa.q: How might Kunal have felt once the umpire watched closely?
qa.a: Kunal probably felt caught out, since he stopped calling bad lines.

grounding: Aditi catches an opponent cheating and feels furious, but tells the umpire calmly instead of cheating back.

passage:
In the village marbles game behind the temple, Afreen saw Asif quietly nudge his marble closer to the line with his toe.
Heat rushed up her neck. She wanted to shout "Cheater!" and scatter his marbles into the dust.
Instead, she took a breath. She walked over to Nizam Chacha, who was sitting on the temple steps and always settled their games.
"Chacha, I think Asif moved his marble with his foot. Can you watch the next round?"
Nizam Chacha came and watched. Asif played the rest fairly, though he glared at her.
Afreen lost the round. But she felt steady. She hadn't turned into a cheater too.

qa.q: How did Afreen feel when she saw Asif cheat?
qa.a: She felt angry, heat rushing up her neck, wanting to shout and scatter his marbles.

qa.q: What did Afreen do that was wise?
qa.a: She told Nizam Chacha calmly instead of accusing Asif loudly or cheating back.

qa.q: How might Asif have felt when Nizam Chacha watched?
qa.a: Asif felt caught and annoyed, glaring at Afreen but playing fairly.

grounding: A girl catches an opponent cheating and feels furious; she tells an adult calmly instead of accusing loudly or cheating back.
